children: South Korea’s current account surplus narrowed to USD 42.08 billion in July 2026, down from a record high of USD 49.73 billion in June.
The goods account surplus fell to USD 40.43 billion in July from USD 47.89 billion in June, with exports soaring 65.3% yoy to USD 100.45 billion, while imports rose 21.7% to USD 60.02 billion.
Exports surged, boosted by strong growth in semiconductor exports amid the global AI boom.
The primary income account surplus increased to USD 4.35 billion from USD 3.27 billion, driven by higher income on equity.
Additionally, the secondary income deficit widened to USD 0.73 billion from USD 0.14 billion, reflecting higher secondary income payments.
Meanwhile, the services account deficit rose to USD 1.97 billion from USD 1.209 billion, due to larger deficits in manufacturing services and the use of intellectual property.
For the 1st seven months of 2026, the current account surplus jumped to USD 233.09 billion from USD 59.82 billion in the same period of 2025.

title: South Korea Current Account Surplus Narrows in July
